A known result gives unitary matrices U and V such that f(A+B)≤Uf(A)U*+Vf(B)V* when f is also monotone. Is that monotonicity assumption actually unnecessary, so that the same unitary-orbit inequality holds for every such concave f?

accepted.question_text: Let A and B be positive definite matrices normalized by Tr(A+B)=1. Does there exist a dimension-independent constant c such that the trace norm of the commutator [B, log(A+B)] is bounded by c times the binary entropy term -Tr A log Tr A - Tr B log Tr B? The source reports numerical evidence that the optimal constant may be c=1.

evidence.quote:
Conjecture 4 Let A, B be positive definite matrices such that Tr(A + B) = 1;
then there is a constant c (independent of the dimensions of A and B) such that
|| [B, log(A + B)] ||1 ≤ c(− Tr A log Tr A − Tr B log Tr B). (26)
Numerical work indicates that c might actually be 1.

Extracted Conjectures 4 and 5 on trace-norm commutator bounds.

Expanded Sendov's conjecture with the polynomial and derivative factorization included.

Expanded the circulant-matrix reformulation into standalone matrix language.
Converted the inverse eigenvalue problem into a full characterization question.
Restated the compression problem with explicit matrix sizes and normality assumptions.
Made the numerical-range functional calculus constant question standalone.
